transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-05 15:00 PDT — Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (LumenTech Procurement), Tina Alvarez (LumenTech Legal), Rohit Singh (LumenTech Security), Maya Ortiz (LumenTech Engineering)
Summary: Procurement/Legal review of Redwood MSA and DPA, discussion of SLAs and audit artifacts, pricing approval path, and vendor onboarding steps. Some transcript artifacts are auto-generated and imperfect. Links referenced: pricing spreadsheet (https://redwood.example/pricing/lumentech-v1), security packet (https://redwood.example/security/lumentech-package), MSA redline doc (sent in follow-up).

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time — appreciate it. quick intro from my side, Samir Patel, account exec on Redwood Inference, and Elena's our solutions engineer who will handle the technical bits.
[00:12] Jared: Jared Kim here from procurement. thanks Samir. we're on a tight cycle so hoping we can cover MSA and DPA redlines and approvals today.
[00:20] Tina: Tina Alvarez, legal — yes, we'll focus on liability caps, data handling, and indemnity.
[00:26] Rohit: Rohit from security, hi. I want to make sure KMS integration, audit logs, and retention requirements are clear.
[00:33] Maya: Maya — engineering lead — i'll be looking at onboarding and pilot SLOs.
[00:38] Elena: great, quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines, 2) SLAs and uptime, 3) security artifacts, 4) pricing and procurement cadence, 5) next steps.

[01:02] Samir: On the MSA we've generally seen the legal teams focus on the indemnity and liability sections — Tina, anything specific you want to call out up front?
[01:15] Tina: Yes, we're pushing for a cap tied to fees for 12 months, and we would prefer more specific data residency and deletion language in the DPA; also wanting clarification on subprocessor lists.
[01:28] Elena: Understood. Redwood's standard practice is to have a fee-based liability cap, we can take that back to legal ops — we do have a redline-friendly MSA PDF we'll send. For DPA, we support region pinning in our private deployments and can state deletion windows — note that behind the scenes on hosted we have configurable retention.
[01:49] Rohit: Do you provide a subprocessor list and do you notify customers before adding new subprocessors?
[01:56] Samir: yes, we maintain a subprocessor list; typically we provide notification, and there's an SLA for notice periods. Elena, correct me if i'm wrong on the timing.
[02:05] Elena: Correct — 30 days' notice for most changes, except emergency patches which we try to minimize. We also have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO 27001 certs — i'll share the artifacts after this call.

[02:28] Tina: On indemnity, there are some standard exceptions we'd expect for open-source model behavior and hallucinations; we want clarity on responsibilities.
[02:38] Samir: Totally reasonable. Our MSA carves out model outputs in specific ways; we can highlight that section. Also worth noting for procurement: for dedicated/private we offer on-prem or VPC options which usually satisfy stricter regs.

[03:05] Jared: Procurement timeline: our board needs vendor sign-off by end of August. Pricing approval is tied to a committed monthly spend vs on-demand. Can you walk through the committed discount tiers?
[03:20] Samir: Sure, short answer: committed reservation gives you a 25% discount at our mid-tier GPU pool, and deeper discounts at annual commitments. We'll send a consolidated spreadsheet with committed vs burst pricing and seat vs token-based examples.
[03:36] Maya: For the pilot, we want deterministic latency under 200ms p95 for our typical prompts. Can you share any benchmarks for similar customers?
[03:45] Elena: yes — we have benchmark sheets; for shorter sequences on dedicated instances we hit ~80–150ms p95 depending on model and quantization. We'll attach a benchmark doc and recommended config (model variant, quantization, batching).

[04:12] Rohit: Regarding encryption: does Redwood support CMK in AWS KMS or customer-managed keys? Also, where are the logs stored and can we forward them to our SIEM?
[04:22] Elena: We support KMS integration and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for Dedicated and Private. Audit logs can be shipped to customer S3, CloudWatch, or third-party SIEMs — retention is configurable.
[04:36] Rohit: Great, also need to confirm if tokens or inputs are stored by default on hosted and what deletion windows are available.
[04:45] Samir: Hosted by default stores short-term transaction logs for debugging and billing, configurable retention down to 7 days in some tiers and longer for compliance packages. DPA can make retention explicit.

[05:05] Tina: Back to SLAs: uptime SLA and remedy is important. What are your standard SLAs and do you offer credits or termination rights on repeated misses?
[05:16] Elena: Our Dedicated product has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has commercial SLA tiers. Remedies are generally service credits for missed availability targets; termination for repeated misses is negotiable but usually tied to cure periods. We'll include SLA language in the MSA redline.

[06:02] Jared: On procurement paperwork — do you accept Net 60? Also need to know if we can get a single consolidated invoice for multiple teams.
[06:12] Samir: We typically accept Net 30 by default, Net 45–60 is possible for enterprise with finance approval. Consolidated invoicing is supported — we'll flag that in the contract.

[06:32] Maya: Technical onboarding: how long to stand up a pilot on dedicated infra? We have a timeline of two weeks for initial test harness.
[06:41] Elena: For Dedicated, once capacity is reserved and infra is provisioned, engineering onboarding is typically 3–10 business days depending on model size; we can prioritize a pilot lane. For Hosted you can spin up in hours.

[07:05] Tina: A question on auditability: do you provide request-level logs with token counts and per-route metrics for compliance?
[07:14] Elena: Yes, we have token-level breakouts, per-route metrics, and tracing hooks to integrate with your observability stack. We'll share dashboard screenshots and an API for query.

[07:40] Jared: Any standard procurement blockers you see from other customers?
[07:45] Samir: main ones are delay on insurance proof, liability cap negotiation, and data residency clauses; having the SOC 2/ISO artifacts and a redline-ready MSA speeds things up a lot.

[08:05] Rohit: About subprocessors again — do you allow review of subprocessors list prior to signing?
[08:11] Samir: We can provide the list and accommodate limited review windows; we try to minimize last-minute surprises.

[09:00] Tina: We might propose one or two redlines around audit rights and on-site inspections; is that something you entertain?
[09:07] Samir: We handle audit requests via secure channels; on-site audits are rarer but possible for Private deployments under stricter contracts. We'll flag that for legal review.

[10:30] Elena: quick note on technical fallbacks: Redwood supports model routing and automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity is constrained — reduces outage risk during spikes.
[10:42] Maya: Good to know — that helps with reliability for UI flows.

[12:00] Jared: On pricing approvals, procurement needs a clean spreadsheet with committed pricing vs example monthly burn so we can present to finance.
[12:09] Samir: we'll provide a template with line items: reserved capacity, overage rates, support add-ons, and data retention/compliance extra costs.

[14:20] Tina: For DPA, do you handle cross-border data transfer language and SCCs?
[14:27] Elena: Yes — we support standard SCCs and can add clauses for data residency where we operate in local regions or with Private deployments.

[16:00] Jared: If procurement signs off by 8/12 can legal complete redlines by 8/18? We're aiming for signature by 8/25.
[16:09] Tina: aggressive but possible, pending a couple of key points on liability and deletion.

[18:30] Samir: To summarize next steps: we'll send the MSA redline PDF, pricing sheet, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, and a proposed pilot runbook. Elena will follow up with technical artifacts.
[18:43] Elena: i'll include benchmark summaries and recommended config for hitting your 200ms p95 target.

[19:10] Rohit: one more security ask — can you provide the encryption in transit details and whether perfect forward secrecy is used?
[19:18] Elena: yes, we use TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers and PFS; details in the security packet i will share.

[20:00] Jared: ok last procurement question — do you have references for customers in our regulated vertical?
[20:07] Samir: We can share anonymized references and case studies in healthcare and finance — some require NDA but we have a couple public writeups.

[21:30] Tina: On the MSA redlines please avoid unilateral audit rights that are too broad; we prefer scoped audit windows.
[21:42] Samir: Understood. We'll propose a scoped audit clause appropriate to your compliance needs.

[25:00] Maya: For onboarding we'll need a runbook and a point-of-contact on your side for infra provisioning.
[25:08] Elena: i'll be the SE point for the pilot and will include a runbook with checklists.

[30:00] (discussion continues with clarifications, occasional crosstalk and filler — some transcription artifacts: "MSA, DPA, SLA" sometimes recognized as "MS P A DPA" in auto-transcript)

[38:00] (Legal and security deepens paragraph-level reading of sample DPA and deletes)

[45:00] Samir: wrapping up — key deliverables from Redwood: pricing spreadsheet, MSA redline PDF, SOC 2/ISO artifacts, benchmark doc, pilot runbook. From LumenTech: procurement timeline confirmation, legal redlines, list of security requirements.

[46:10] Jared: we'll aim to review the materials and get back with procurement approval window by Aug 12.
[46:18] Tina: legal will circulate redlines within 5 business days of receiving the redline MSA.

[47:00] Samir: perfect, i'll send the follow-ups end of day. thank you everyone.
[47:07] Elena: thanks all.
[47:10] Meeting ended.
